title: Continents Move at Fingernail Speed
post_title: Continents Move at Fingernail Speed | QuantaTale
post_description: The ground beneath continents is moving—and often at about the speed your fingernails grow. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/how-fast-do-tectonic-plates-move https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/dynamic/understanding.html #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Earth's outer shell is divided into enormous tectonic plates. They move relative to one another, but usually not at a speed you can feel. The US Geological Survey compares typical plate motion to the rate that fingernails grow. Different plates move at different speeds and in different directions. Scientists measure this motion with satellite-based GPS. Over millions of years, that slow movement reshapes oceans, builds mountains and helps explain where earthquakes occur.
